author: Alex Rivera
text: Great breakdown of the small-training-population problem. Did you compare against a straight pedigree BLUP baseline?

author: Jane Doe
text: Yes, pedigree BLUP is included as the baseline in Figure 2 — genomic models only pull ahead once the training set clears a few hundred individuals.

author: Alex Rivera
text: That matches what we've seen in our own herd. Thanks for confirming.

author: Priya Nair
text: Curious whether marker density mattered as much as raw sample size here.

author: Sam Okafor
text: Fertility heritability being that noisy tracks with what we see across management systems, not just genetics.

author: Jane Doe
text: Agreed — we tried to control for herd-year effects but there's still a lot of unexplained variance left.

author: Priya Nair
text: Would love to see this repeated with a larger hidden layer once more records come in.

author: Alex Rivera
text: How many flights per week were needed to keep the NDVI series useful?

author: Jane Doe
text: Weekly was enough for us, but during irrigation season we bumped it to twice a week.

author: Sam Okafor
text: Good to know — planning a similar setup for next season.

author: Sam Okafor
text: Interesting that the old heuristic held up at all after a decade of drift in the herd.
